statement: The first line holds n and k; the second holds n integers, each sitting at most k positions away from its place in the sorted order. Print the fully sorted array, space-separated. Exploit the promise with a min-heap over a sliding window of k+1 elements: push the first k+1 values, then repeatedly pop the minimum into the output and push the next array element. The true next value is always inside the window, so the output comes out sorted in n log k time.

example.why: Every element is within three slots of home, so the smallest of any k+1 window is the next output.

hint: Heap size k+1, no larger - the promise guarantees the minimum of the window is globally next.
mistake: Sorting the whole array from scratch; right answer, but it pays n log n and ignores the gift.
